result.rationale: Flag a present source-level code/policy conflict and retain the complete authored instruction without edits. Before code reads an id directly from Style; after code calls GetKmlStyleId, which also accepts the wrapping CascadingStyle id and passes that style into ParseKmlStyle. This can change resolved styles written in stored vskg_options for affected KML/KMZ sources. CurrentConversionVersion remains 1 in both snapshots. GetCurrentVersionRows selects version-1 rows and ShouldConvertLayer skips conversion when converted rows already exist; ConvertLayerForJob skips conversion and returns whether converted rows exist. Consequently an already-converted affected file can retain the older result until its rows are cleared, despite the current instruction requiring a version increment when stored style interpretation can differ. The current rule is relevant and should be preserved; implementation behavior is not an accepted reason to weaken it. Propose a separately reviewed code correction from CurrentConversionVersion 1 to 2, subject to current dependency revalidation and an affected previously-converted-file check; this instruction proposal applies no code or policy change. Temporal qualification: the complete requested-base instruction has no KML/KMZ Conversion Version section, while current guidance does. Read-only historical inspection identifies the style fix as PR2067 and the later version instruction as PR2075. This is a present conflict, not a finding that PR2067 violated a then-existing version instruction or a complete historical shipping replay. The packet supports the literal source-path mechanism; it does not establish production cached rows, deployment state, observed user impact, or end-to-end reconversion behavior. Known linked and symbol coverage gaps remain explicit and prevent a whole-feature compliance claim.
